messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: how to get
parts:
Your example looks fairly simple. 

x data would be your variables. (e.g. points per game)
y data would be the value of those variables (without scaling this might not work very well)
The color could be specified by another variable.

Facet by team and you're there. 

dataframe would be in this structure

bball<-structure(list(Team = structure(c(1L, 1L, 1L, 2L, 2L, 2L), .Label = c("Dallas", 
"Miami"), class = "factor"), Variable = structure(c(2L, 3L, 1L, 
2L, 3L, 1L), .Label = c("Dunks", "PPG", "Rebounds"), class = "factor"), 
    Value = c(90L, 15L, 20L, 90L, 25L, 10L), Col = c(1L, 2L, 
    1L, 2L, 1L, 2L)), .Names = c("Team", "Variable", "Value", 
"Col"), class = "data.frame", row.names = c(NA, -6L))

ggplot(bball, aes(x=Variable, y=Value, fill=as.factor(Col)))+geom_bar()+facet_grid(Team~.)

Unless I'm missing something?

Brandon

You can reduce the space with an Option....


#no margins
plot + opts(panel.margin=unit(0 , "lines"))

No idea on the black line. Probably can do it with a grob, but that is beyond my skills.

B
